ASP ratios 0.8739 (Mvasi) and 0.8818 (Kanjinti), mean 0.8778. $81,812.93 x 0.8778 = $71,815
column12: Judgement on construction, as in amgn_abp_206.csv: Keytruda's Part B figure scaled by the net-to-net (ASP) ratio Amgen's own IV oncology biosimilars took in Medicare in their first full year, so that the house Part B deduction in gross_to_net_pct lands the net on the biosimilar's ASP, $67,750. It is not ABP 234's own Medicare allowed amount, which would carry an add-on on the reference's ASP. The 2024 annual figure was $79,464 ($5,988,521,233 over 75,361, drug_demand), so 2025 is 3.0% higher; no inflation to the 2029 launch is applied. A beneficiary's spend covers about 0.41 of a year's labelled dose (see discontinuation_pct), so this is a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug. Price erosion after launch is carried separately in net_price_decline_pct. The case for lower: ten developers entering at one date is a more crowded first wave than either analogue faced, so the launch discount may be deeper than 12%

column10: share of the treated stock stopping per year
column11: drug_demand Keytruda, CMS Part B 2024, the latest year that carries dosage units (the 2025 quarterly file has none): 107,476,784 dosage units over 75,361 beneficiaries = 1,426 mg per beneficiary. HCPCS J9271 is 'injection, pembrolizumab, 1 mg'. A full labelled year is 3,467 mg (200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks over 52 weeks; Keytruda USPI), so a beneficiary averages 0.4114 of a year on drug, and 1 - 0.4114 = 0.5886. The ratio is stable across 2020 to 2024 (0.380, 0.394, 0.407, 0.407, 0.411)
column12: Judgement on method, as in amgn_abp_206.csv. The pool is Keytruda's own patients across every indication, so this is measured on them rather than taken from one lung cancer trial's median. Under a constant hazard in a steady state, the share of a year's treated patients still on drug into the next year equals the patient-years per beneficiary, 0.411, so the engine's stock is the count of beneficiaries the per-beneficiary price is quoted on. The implied hazard is 0.89 a year, a median time on drug of 9.4 months. eligible_pct is built from this value (new starts = treated patients x 0.5886), so changing one without the other moves the steady-state patient count. The case against: dose holds and the 2 mg/kg paediatric dose lower mg per patient-year and overstate stopping; the 24-month and one-year caps in the label mean a patient who stays well still stops, which a constant hazard spreads evenly

column11: Merck FY2025 10-K (0000310158-26-000063, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310158/000031015826000063/mrk-20251231.htm): 'while two patents in the Keytruda composition of matter patent family expire in May and November of 2029, respectively, the Company expects these patents to be the subject of litigation and, thus, biosimilar competition could begin in December 2028 when the primary compound patent expires'. The book carries this as Keytruda's US loss of exclusivity, 2028-12-31 (biologic_loe, asset 412, 10-K disclosure). The earliest Phase 3 primary completion is NCT06430866, 2026-12-14 (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, estimated), which plus two gives 2028, but a biosimilar cannot enter before the reference's exclusivity ends, so launch is December 2028 and 2029 is the first full year on sale
column12: Judgement on the month: Merck names December 2028 as the earliest and Amgen gives no launch date. The case for later: the two 2029 composition-of-matter patents Merck expects to litigate, and the method-of-use patents a BPCIA exchange could assert, could hold entry to late 2029 or force carve-outs; no Keytruda BPCIA suit or settlement is on record as of 2026-10-12. Amgen's NCT06311721 does not complete until 2028-01-10, though the PK study reads out in December 2026 and FDA's October 2025 draft guidance lets a PK study carry a filing. The case for earlier: none, since the 12-year reference product exclusivity (2026-09-04, book exclusivities row) is already past and the patent sets the date

column11: Keytruda's new IV patient starts a year in the US, 125,609, over the book's 192,650 = 0.6520. Built from (1) Merck FY2025 10-K (0000310158-26-000063) US sales: Keytruda $18,829mm and Keytruda Qlex $38mm, $18,867mm of pembrolizumab. Over Keytruda's 2025 Part B figure on an ASP basis ($81,812.93 / 1.06 = $77,182, the list_price_per_patient anchor) that is 244,448 US patients treated in the year, on the same per-beneficiary basis the price is quoted on. Medicare fee-for-service is 77,692 of these, 32%. (2) The IV share, by the book's Keytruda Qlex convention (mrk_keytruda_qlex.csv and keytruda.csv share_plateau): Keytruda Qlex's US share taken to 12.7%, the share Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo Qvantig held of its US franchise in its sixth quarter (BMS Q2 2026 8-K 0000014272-26-000018: Qvantig US $206mm, Opdivo US $1,417mm), so 87.3% of US pembrolizumab patients stay on the IV form a biosimilar can substitute for. 244,448 x 0.873 = 213,403. (3) New starts are the treated count x discontinuation_pct: 213,403 x 0.5886 = 125,609
column12: The pool is Keytruda's own IV-treated patients, not a disease. A biosimilar takes the reference product's patients across every labelled indication it is extrapolated to (lung, melanoma, head and neck, bladder, kidney, breast, gastro-oesophageal, cervical, endometrial and others), not the NSCLC population its similarity trials enrolled. NSCLC is used only because the indication must be one of the asset's own. The share is a scaling of the book's NSCLC incidence to Keytruda's IV new starts, not an NSCLC eligibility filter. Check: 213,403 x $77,182 = $16,471mm, 87.3% of FY2025 US pembrolizumab sales, so the pool reproduces the reference's IV revenue at its own net price. The case for lower: Keytruda Qlex already held 7.9% of US pembrolizumab in Q2 2026, its fourth quarter on sale ($395mm against Keytruda $4,611mm, 8-K 0001104659-26-090045), ahead of Qvantig's 6.3% at the same point, and the convention is a floor that Merck has two more years to push past before the cliff. The case for higher: Merck's net revenue per patient sits below ASP because of Medicaid rebates and 340B, so the count understates patients, and the IV pool is held at its 2025 size although US Keytruda grew 5.4% in 2025 ($17,872mm to $18,829mm, same 10-K)

column11: Fitted on the engine's own identity (line-of-therapy pool, discontinuation_pct 0.5886, logistic ramp) to ABP 234's even slice of the measured biosimilar class path. (1) The class path: the biosimilars' share of IV dosage units in Medicare Part B for the three oncology antibodies that have faced biosimilars, each in its first five full years (2020 to 2024), from the CMS Medicare Part B Spending by Drug dataset (data.cms.gov dataset 76a714ad-3a2c-43ac-b76d-9dadf8f7d890, every Q5 biosimilar code against the reference's J code; the subcutaneous and conjugate forms left out). Trastuzumab 34.7%, 61.9%, 72.4%, 77.9%, 79.9%; rituximab 19.1%, 47.3%, 57.2%, 61.6%, 64.0%; bevacizumab 36.3%, 63.0%, 75.3%, 80.2%, 84.7%; mean 30.0%, 57.4%, 68.3%, 73.2%, 76.2%. (2) The slice: one tenth, for the ten developers with an active or completed comparative clinical study against Keytruda whose primary completion falls before the 2028 loss of exclusivity (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-12): Samsung Bioepis SB27 (NCT06348199, 2026-03), Sandoz GME751 (NCT06159790 and NCT06153238, completed 2026-03 and 2026-05), Formycon FYB206 (NCT06551064, 2026-06), mAbxience MB12 (NCT06687369, 2026-08), Amgen (NCT06430866, 2026-12), Celltrion CT-P51 (NCT06939595, 2027-02), Bio-Thera BAT3306 (NCT07180862, 2027-02), Henlius HLX17 (NCT07160335, 2027-04), Alvotech AVT32-DRL_PB (NCT07475572, 2027-10) and Biocon Bmab1800 (NCT07581509, 2027-12). Slice path 3.00%, 5.74%, 6.83%, 7.32%, 7.62%. (3) Fit: peak 0.077, k 3.8, midpoint -0.18 reproduce it as 3.01%, 5.72%, 6.88%, 7.36%, 7.56% of the treated pool, RMSE 0.04 points, settling at 7.7%
column12: Judgements, three. (1) An even slice, because Amgen's own record across its four Part B biosimilars averages one: its share of each molecule's biosimilar units in 2024, times the number of biosimilars billed, is 1.74 for Mvasi (first of four), 1.19 for Kanjinti (first of five), 0.69 for Riabni (third of three) and 0.37 for Avsola (third of three in infliximab), mean 1.00 (same CMS dataset). Its two first movers launched months before any rival; here every developer waits for one date, so no first-mover premium is taken. (2) Ten entrants. Counting developers by a registered study is the amgn_abp_692.csv method; studies of PK alone are counted because FDA's October 2025 draft guidance ('Scientific Considerations in Demonstrating Biosimilarity to a Reference Product: Updated Recommendations for Assessing the Need for Comparative Efficacy Studies', 2025-10-29) lets a PK similarity study carry most filings. The case for higher: only three to five biosimilars entered each oncology analogue, and the two latest readouts here (Alvotech, Biocon) may be approved after the cliff; at five entrants the share doubles. The case for lower: Qilu's QL2107 gained a US partner in Cipla on 2026-09-03 (Goodwin, Big Molecule Watch, 2026-09-15) and is not counted, since its registry records are not yet recruiting or of unknown status. (3) The class path's first year had five months of launch before it (July 2019 entry), where pembrolizumab biosimilars enter in December 2028, so the modelled 2029 may run ahead of the analogue. Cross-check: Liu et al. (JAMA Oncol 2026, doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2026.3128, PMID 42658505) find the three reference products' Medicare Part B share fell 31.5% a year after biosimilar entry, a class share of 31.5%, 53.1% and 67.9% by year three, within two points of the path above until year four
